Article Title: Oracle founder Larry Ellison believes America is on right track with AI, he sees robots taking jobs, and says what is needed is right taxation system
Article Text:
“We need to change from taxing human labour to taxing value added,”

“So when the robots add value, all that value that the robots add is taxed, and we could have

universal high income

.”

How robots could reduce costs while replacing some jobs

“kind of nonsensical”

How would universal high income work

“reverse income tax”

Larry Ellison believes AI can make everyone wealthier. The Oracle co-founder and chief technology officer says robots will take over some jobs, but argues that greater productivity and changes to taxation could help spread the resulting wealth. Speaking at Oracle AI World in Las Vegas, he described a future in which automation reduces the cost of goods and services while US governments collect revenue from the value machines create.he said.His argument links AI’s economic benefits to how governments distribute them, with less reliance on taxing people’s work.Ellison rejected the suggestion that AI would eventually replace everyone, calling that prediction. However, he acknowledged that automation would displace some workers, pointing to rideshare services as an example.He argued that better tools could also allow people to accomplish more. In the supplied account of his remarks, he cited robotic surgeons and aircraft autopilot systems to illustrate how technology can change work and improve productivity.To explain the potential effect on prices, Ellison described a hypothetical house built entirely by robots. If human labour previously accounted for 80% of its cost, he suggested, automating construction could substantially reduce that expense.The example illustrated his prediction about cheaper production; it was not a reported result from an actual housing project.Ellison’s proposal centres on taxing the economic value generated by automation and using that revenue to support people’s incomes. Universal basic income generally means regular payments intended to cover essential living costs. The universal high income he described would go further, relying on AI-driven productivity to support higher living standards even as machines do more of the work.He also referred to economist Milton Friedman’s negative income tax proposal, describing it as a. Broadly, such a system pays people whose incomes fall below a specified threshold. Ellison’s comments outlined a possible direction for taxation rather than a detailed policy. The supplied excerpts do not specify tax rates, payment amounts, or eligibility rules.He acknowledged that the transition would take more than a decade, with robots gradually taking on more tasks people don't want to do.
Article Summary: Larry Ellison believes AI can make everyone wealthier. Oracle co-founder and chief technology officer says robots will take over some jobs, but argues that greater productivity and changes to taxation could help spread the resulting wealth. He described a future in which automation reduces the cost of goods and services while US governments collect revenue from the value machines create.

Article Title: As IPO nears, Claude-maker Anthropic is set to make hundreds of employees millionaires; and it is worrying CEO Dario Amodei, making HR ask new hires: If ...
Article Text:
IPO could create a new class of AI millionaires

The interview question

Dario Amodei's concern: Mission over money

The talent war

Wealth concentration worries AI leaders

As AI giant Anthropic moves closer to a blockbuster initial public offering that could value the company between $1.5 trillion and $2 trillion, the Claude-maker is poised to create a new wave of wealthy tech employees. But while the potential windfall could mint hundreds of employee millionaires, it is also creating an unusual concern for CEO Dario Amodei, according to a report by Fortune. The company is reportedly asking prospective employees during culture interviews how they would react if Anthropic abandoned its AI ambitions for safety reasons and the company's stock subsequently fell to zero. The unusual question is designed to gauge whether candidates are motivated primarily by the company's mission or by the prospect of financial gains from a future IPO. According to a report cited by Fortune, one candidate said they told interviewers they would not be happy if the stock became worthless, but would want to balance ethical goals with building a sustainable business.Anthropic is targeting a November IPO that could value the company as high as $2 trillion, potentially surpassing the record-setting public debut of SpaceX, Fortune reported. With more than 2,500 employees and stock-based compensation widely used across the company, such a valuation could generate massive wealth for current staff.The prospect of hundreds of employees becoming millionaires appears to be raising concerns among company leaders, particularly as Anthropic attempts to maintain its identity as an AI safety-focused organisation rather than a traditional high-growth technology company.Anthropic is reportedly asking job candidates in culture interviews how they would feel if the company someday dropped its AI ambitions for safety reasons and the decision sent its stock to zero, according to Axios. One candidate who described the process on the anonymous workplace site Blind said they were honest and would not be happy if the stock went to zero, adding that they would want to combine doing the most good and staying ethical with building a sustainable business.CEO Dario Amodei, whose net worth is estimated at $13.6 billion, has reportedly expressed concern about how the company’s huge financial incentives could affect its ability to retain employees who are truly committed to its mission. Anthropic is a public benefit corporation and has long tried to set itself apart from rivals such as OpenAI by focusing on AI safety and the long-term benefit of humanity. Its values statement says the mission is what everyone is there for.Anthropic has long distinguished itself from rivals by emphasising AI safety and what it describes as the "long-term benefit of humanity." As a public benefit corporation, the company's mission plays a central role in its culture and decision-making. Fortune reports that Amodei, whose own estimated net worth stands at roughly $13.6 billion, has expressed concerns that enormous financial incentives could make it harder to identify and retain employees who genuinely believe in the company's mission. The firm's values statement emphasises that its mission should be the guiding force behind decisions rather than competing financial motivations.The reported interview question reflects that concern by asking candidates to consider a scenario where the company prioritises safety over commercial success, even if doing so destroys shareholder value.Anthropic is competing with Meta, Google, Microsoft and OpenAI for top researchers and engineers. In its S-1 filing, dated October 26, the company acknowledged that hiring and retaining qualified staff on competitive terms has become exceptionally difficult and has intensified significantly, particularly in the San Francisco Bay Area, where it is headquartered.Fortune says Anthropic is currently offering base salaries of $350,000 to $850,000 for staff software engineering roles. It has more than 600 open positions, including about 120 in sales, more than 60 in AI research and engineering, and 50 in security. Some candidates are reportedly spending more than $4,000 on private coaching to improve their chances, and Aline Lerner, founder of the prep company Interviewing.io, told Bloomberg that the maths works when a few thousand dollars can raise a salary by $200,000.The potential wealth creation at Anthropic comes amid broader concerns about the economic impact of the AI boom. Amodei has previously warned that artificial intelligence could concentrate wealth among a relatively small group of people if safeguards are not put in place. Earlier this year, Amodei and Anthropic's six other co-founders, including his sister Daniela Amodei, committed to giving away 80% of their wealth. In a public letter, Amodei argued that excessive wealth concentration could "break society" and said wealthy individuals have a responsibility to help address inequality that may be worsened by AI.As Anthropic prepares for what could be one of the largest public offerings in technology history, the company finds itself balancing two competing realities: attracting top talent with lucrative pay packages and stock grants, while ensuring employees remain committed to the safety-focused mission that has defined the company since its founding.
Article Summary: Anthropic is reportedly asking job candidates in culture interviews how they would feel if the company abandoned its AI ambitions for safety reasons. The unusual question is designed to gauge whether candidates are motivated primarily by the company's mission or by the prospect of financial gains from a future IPO. CEO Dario Amodei has reportedly expressed concern about how the company’s huge financial incentives could affect its ability to retain employees who are truly committed to its mission.

Article Title: Why basic phones are holding on in the age of AI smartphones
Article Text:
कंपनी 8 अक्टूबर से शुरू हो रही फ्लिपकार्ट बिग बिलियन डेज सेल में स्मार्टफोन को बेचेगी।

New Delhi: India’s basic phone is refusing to hang up. As rising smartphone prices put upgrades beyond some buyers’ budgets, feature-phone manufacturers are adding digital payments and other services to devices whose biggest attractions remain affordability, battery life and simplicity. The pressure on smartphone affordability has intensified since September. Counterpoint Research’s October 23 report showed shipments below Rs 20,000 falling 47% year-on-year in July–September, partly because price increases pushed models into higher bands. Overall smartphone shipments declined 20%. That does not establish a shift towards feature phones, but it provides a sharper backdrop to why their users may postpone upgrading.Arijeet Talapatra, CEO of itel India, Transsion Holdings, described the feature-phone category as increasingly driven by replacement demand. Affordability remains the biggest draw, alongside durability, multi-day battery life and ease of use.“Feature phones continue to serve a distinct and practical need: they offer reliable, essential connectivity at a price and level of simplicity that smartphones cannot always replicate,” he said.Ravi Kunwar, vice-president and CEO, HMD India and APAC, estimated that around 200 million people still use 2G feature phones. That represents an existing user base, rather than annual handset sales.“Consumers are looking for better connectivity and more features, but that does not always mean they want to move to a smartphone,” Kunwar said.Digital payments are expanding what compatible basic handsets can do. PhonePe announced its UPI 123Pay service on August 31, using an SMS-based system that does not require mobile internet. Its current terms allow transfers, merchant payments and QR scanning on camera-equipped feature phones, with one bank account enabled at a time.At launch, PhonePe named Nokia, HMD, Lava and itel as handset partners. It also announced an activation helpline supporting English and 12 Indian languages. Bill payments, recharges and Aadhaar-based onboarding were described as forthcoming; their rollout needs confirmation before being presented as available.More capabilities, however, have not produced consistent shipment growth. CMR’s April–June 2026 data showed 2G feature-phone shipments rising 5% year-on-year while 4G models declined 43%. Itel held 38% of the 2G segment, followed by Lava at 30% and HMD at 20%. These are second-quarter figures, not a measure of current festive demand.Talapatra nevertheless expects migration towards 4G to accelerate. He said itel was expanding digital-payment support and larger displays, while inexpensive 2G handsets retained a role as backup calling devices.HMD similarly sees better connectivity and payments as ways to extend the category’s usefulness. Older users value familiar controls, while some smartphone owners want a break from notifications and social media. Kunwar identified digital detox as another reason for buying basic phones, although he provided no figures establishing its scale.For manufacturers, the task is to make these devices more useful while preserving the low cost and simplicity that keep customers buying them.
Article Summary: Rising smartphone prices put upgrades beyond some buyers’ budgets. Counterpoint Research’s October 23 report showed shipments below Rs 20,000 falling 47% year- on-year in July–September. Around 200 million people still use 2G feature phones in India.

Article Title: IIT Kharagpur highlights success of Nagar Udyam initiative through campus pilot
Article Text: The Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Kharagpur has highlighted the success of its Nagar Udyam initiative that was launched as a pilot within the campus during Durga Puja this year.This is a pioneering solar-powered smart street vending initiative, conceptualised by Prof. Suman Chakraborty, Director, IIT Kharagpur, through its SETU Cloud Kitchen Connect.The aim is to popularise the concept among micro-entrepreneurs, allowing them to do business in a sustainable manner.This model allows a business to start without renting a shop, building permanent infrastructure or occupying roadside space after working hours.It enables an entrepreneur to take an entire business home at night and move it towards customers the next morning.Apart from Prof. Chakraborty, Siddharth Singh Dangi, SDPO, Kharagpur and several others, including small entrepreneurs, were present during the inauguration of the project. This is part of the institute's Platinum Jubilee commitment to translate design and technology into tangible social and economic opportunities.The project involves a small three-wheeled cart that can be towed by the owner's motorcycle. This will enable the entrepreneur to move to where there is demand. It has a range of about 30 km, subject to operational and road-safety validation.Once the day's business is done, the home-storage unit can be taken home, thereby clearing up public road space. The cart has solar-cum-battery renewal-energy-enabled essential low-power functions, with compact battery storage.The carts have the SETU digital backbone, including QR-enabled identification, cashless payments, training and pathways to financial inclusion. They also have built-in hygiene, with protected food display, food-grade surfaces and three-way waste segregation.Through the campus demonstration, IIT Kharagpur hopes to replicate the model across West Bengal, allowing street vendors to operate with dignity, without getting into trouble with the authorities.The compact vending structure can be towed by the owner behind a motorcycle, positioned at suitable places of concentrated demand and taken back home after business hours.A vendor could potentially cater to commuters in one part of the day and to a campus or community gathering later, without being tied to a costly permanent storefront. Its proposed mobility over roughly 30 kilometres offers a route to wider customer access.This changes the equation for both livelihoods and urban space. Rather than treating the entrepreneur’s business and pedestrian accessibility as competing priorities, the design aims for flexible, appropriately authorised vending that does not permanently claim a portion of the road.Further envisaged elements include food-safety status access, grievance redressal and data-assisted governance.“Our ambition is not simply to redesign a street cart; it is to redesign the opportunity around the person who runs it. A business that can move with demand, return home at night and connect to clean energy and digital finance can turn an opportunity seeker into a job creator. That is the kind of technology translation IIT Kharagpur stands for," Prof Chakraborty had said during the launch.The initiative suggests a fresh approach to public-space management: vending with clearer identification, better food practices, mobility and reduced permanent obstruction. These benefits will depend on practical traffic safeguards, lawful operating locations and coordination with civic authorities.As stated by Shri Siddharth Singh Dangi, SDPO, Kharagpur, “The best solutions for our streets must protect livelihoods as well as public safety. A mobile, identifiable and responsibly operated vending unit offers an interesting way to reduce permanent obstruction while preserving economic opportunity. The key will be disciplined implementation, safe movement and compliance with local rules.”The launch at the IIT Kharagpur campus evaluated food safety, operational efficiency, environmental performance, mobility, vendor experience and consumer response.Evidence from the pilot is intended to inform a prospective West Bengal Smart Street Vendor Framework, covering cart standards, food-safety practices, space management and measurable social outcomes. In this micro-startup vision, someone who cannot afford a permanent shop may still be able to build a business — and, over time, create jobs for others.
Article Summary: Nagar Udyam is a pioneering solar-powered smart street vending initiative. The aim is to popularise the concept among micro-entrepreneurs. This model allows a business to start without renting a shop, building permanent infrastructure or occupying roadside space after working hours.

Article Title: Trust remains one of the biggest factors driving consumers to physical electronics stores: Gaurav Pahwa, MD, Lotus Electronics
Article Text:
Gaurav Pahwa is managing director Lotus Electronics

Q. The RAM crisis has increased prices of smartphones, how has that impacted buying trends?

Q. Is there a noticeable shift towards consumers choosing premium products across categories?

Q. Which categories do you expect to see maximum consumer interest and store visits this festive season?

Q. Tell us about any noticeable differences in footfall, consumer preferences or category demand across markets where Lotus operates?

Gaurav Pahwa is managing director Lotus Electronics, a leading electronics retail chain in Central India. Backed by a 26-year legacy, the brand has 30 retail stores across nine cities. Pahwa, who holds a postgraduate degree in Business Management from the University of Kent, joined the family business in 2003. In an interaction he shared electronic buying trends this festive season, how RAM crisis has impacted gadget buying and more. Excerpts:Yes, component costs have gone up, and this has had an impact on smartphone pricing, but we are not seeing customers hold back from their purchases. In fact, some consumers are choosing to buy faster because they expect prices to rise further, particularly those who have already identified the model they want. This has made the timing of the purchase more important, as customers would rather make their purchase now than risk paying a higher price later. At the same time, consumers continue to look at the overall value of the smartphone and the features it offers rather than focusing only on the increase in upfront pricing.Performance, features and the overall experience remain important parts of the decision. This is where our finance and EMI options are playing a particularly important role.So, while higher component costs are influencing smartphone prices, we are not seeing a corresponding slowdown in buying intent. Consumers continue to upgrade, and financing is helping them manage the purchase more comfortably.Yes, premiumisation has been a growing trend over the past few festive seasons, and we are seeing it increasingly across categories. Customers are buying fewer products, but they are choosing better ones when they do make a purchase. Whether it is a bigger television, a better laptop or a full-size refrigerator, consumers are increasingly willing to invest more when they believe the product will offer stronger performance, better technology or greater utility over a longer period. This tells us that the purchase decision is becoming less about simply replacing an existing product and more about making a considered investment for the future. We are also seeing this behaviour extend beyond one particular category, with customers evaluating premium products across televisions, smartphones, laptops and appliances.At Lotus Electronics, our extended warranty plans also give customers greater confidence to move towards premium products. Knowing that they are covered well beyond the standard warranty period provides an additional layer of assurance when making a higher-value purchase. Overall, we believe the combination of stronger product expectations, long-term value, financing flexibility and extended protection is encouraging consumers to move towards premium choices.We expect large-screen TVs, premium smartphones and major appliances such as refrigerators, washing machines and ACs to attract the maximum consumer interest and store visits this festive season. These are categories where consumers often plan their purchases in advance, particularly when they are looking to upgrade their homes or replace existing products. Within televisions, larger screen sizes and premium models are expected to see strong interest as consumers increasingly look for a better viewing experience. Premium smartphones will also remain an important category as customers continue to look for better performance, features and overall user experience. Among appliances, refrigerators, washing machines and ACs are expected to benefit from festive demand as consumers evaluate both replacement and upgrade purchases.Laptops are also gaining popularity, while premium audio products such as soundbars and headphones are increasingly being considered as festive gifting options.Alongside the category demand, the overall purchase proposition will play an important role in driving conversions. We are running strong cashback offers on card purchases through the season, and these offers can encourage customers who are already considering a purchase to move towards a final decision. We typically see such benefits helping customers finalise their purchases in-store rather than continuing to wait. Overall, we expect a healthy combination of festive gifting, planned purchases and upgrade-led demand across these key categories.Yes, each city is a little different, and we do see noticeable variations in footfall, consumer preferences and category demand across our markets. In a few of our more mature markets, we see stronger demand for premium and lifestyle products, where customers are more willing to explore higher-value options. In other cities, appliances and TVs lead the way, often linked to weddings and new homes being set up. Some markets also show a healthy mix of smartphones and large appliances, reflecting a combination of personal technology upgrades and household purchases. These variations are important because customer requirements and buying priorities are not identical across markets. Consumers in different cities can have different needs depending on what they are upgrading and the type of purchase they are planning.At the same time, there are some common behaviours that we see across our markets. Customers are becoming increasingly research-oriented, spending more time comparing products and evaluating their options before making a decision. What stays constant across every market is our 6C philosophy: ‘Comfort, Convenience, Choice, Competitive rates, Care and Commitment’. This remains the foundation of how we serve customers and ensures that the quality of the customer experience remains consistent, regardless of which city they are in.Q. Despite e-commerce growth, what drives consumers to physical stores during the festive period?Trust remains one of the biggest factors driving consumers to physical electronics stores, along with the opportunity to see and experience the product before making a purchase. For big-ticket items such as televisions and appliances, customers want to touch the product, compare different models and understand the differences before deciding. This kind of physical experience is difficult to replicate completely online, particularly when customers are making a significant investment. The physical store also gives consumers access to expert advice, which becomes important when they are comparing brands, specifications, features and different models.Our after-sales support also plays a significant role in building confidence, particularly when customers are investing in big-ticket products. For many consumers, the purchase does not end once the transaction is completed; they also want to know that they will have support afterwards. This is why the physical store continues to remain relevant despite the growth of e-commerce. Customers know that they are not just buying a product, but also getting trust, expert assistance, after-sales support and peace of mind throughout the ownership journey.
Article Summary: Gaurav Pahwa is managing director Lotus Electronics, a leading electronics retail chain in Central India. Backed by a 26-year legacy, the brand has 30 retail stores across nine cities. In an interaction he shared electronic buying trends this festive season, how RAM crisis has impacted gadget buying and more.

Article Title: Daylight saving time 2026 ends in the US: Clocks fall back an hour, and sleep experts aren't happy
Article Text:
AI-generated image for representation

Donald Trump's permanent daylight saving time push is stuck in the Senate

Sleep experts and most Americans would rather keep standard time

Most of the US turned its clocks back by an hour on Sunday, November 1, as daylight saving time ended for 2026. The switch happened at 2 am local time, the night after Halloween, giving millions an extra hour of sleep and much darker evenings until mid-March.The change comes as President Donald Trump pushes to make daylight saving time permanent. Sleep experts also want to scrap the twice-yearly switch, just not the way the White House does. They prefer permanent standard time, the very clock Americans returned to this weekend.Smartphones update on their own, but ovens, microwaves and car dashboards need a manual reset. Hawaii and most of Arizona skip DST, so their clocks stayed put, as did US territories like Puerto Rico and Guam. The Navajo Nation in Arizona does switch to match its communities in New Mexico and Utah.The difference shows quickly. Boston's sun set at 5:39 pm on Saturday and at 4:37 pm on Sunday, according to the National Weather Service.For Indians, the gap with the US East Coast widens to 10.5 hours from 9.5, and with the West Coast to 13.5 hours from 12.5. The New York Stock Exchange now opens at 8 pm IST instead of 7 pm.The House passed the Sunshine Protection Act with bipartisan support in July.It would keep clocks on DST all year, meaning later winter sunrises and sunsets, while letting states opt out of daylight saving time entirely.The bill has stalled in the Senate, where Arkansas Republican Tom Cotton leads the opposition. In October, Trump accused Cotton of blocking it and posted the senator's cellphone number on social media, urging people to call him. Cotton pointed out that the US had tried permanent DST before and dropped it after people faced "absurdly late sunrises in the winter."That attempt came in 1974, during the energy crisis, and was reversed within a year over concerns about children going to school in the dark.The American Academy of Sleep Medicine backs permanent standard time as it aligns better with the body's natural sleep cycle. Experts warn that darker mornings and brighter evenings can throw off sleep, and permanent DST would send millions of children to school before sunrise.Public opinion leans the same way. A Gallup survey found 48% of Americans favour permanent standard time, against 24% who want permanent DST.Time is also running out for the bill. All pending legislation expires in early January, when lawmakers elected in Tuesday's midterms take office. If it dies, both chambers start over.So for now, the sleep experts have the clock they prefer. That lasts until March 14, 2027, when Americans spring forward again, an unusually late date because March begins on a Monday.
Article Summary: Most of the US turned its clocks back by an hour on Sunday, November 1, as daylight saving time ended for 2026. The switch happened at 2 am local time, the night after Halloween, giving millions an extra hour of sleep and much darker evenings until mid-March. Sleep experts also want to scrap the twice-yearly switch.

Article Title: SpaceX has stopped taking bookings beyond 2028 for its Falcon 9 rockets, and this means a 'huge problem' for satellite companies in Canada as investors ask …
Article Text:
Elon Musk SpaceX

“That’s a huge problem for the industry,”

What are investors asking Canadian satellite companies

“I think this is the first time where we’ve had serious questions from investors about, ‘You have all these plans—that’s great. How are you going to launch all these satellites?’”

Why Telesat still needs SpaceX

“For us to be competitive, all of our cost inputs need to be world-class competitive,”

How close is a Canadian alternative

“I’ve got the designs already for the facility and flame trenches and buildings and everything else,”

“We could start construction tomorrow. I just need a rocket to put there.”

Elon Musk’s SpaceX has reportedly stopped accepting launch bookings from Canadian companies. The reported cutoff concerns Falcon 9 missions beyond 2028, as the company prepares to shift towards its larger Starship rocket. For Canadian satellite companies seeking investment to expand, the uncertainty is said to be prompting investors to question how their planned satellites will reach orbit.Kepler CEO Mina Mitry warned that reduced access to shared rocket launches could make it harder for smaller companies to launch experimental satellites.he told The Logic. Canada’s own rocket developers remain years away from offering the launch capacity needed to deploy large satellite networks.At the SpaceBound conference in Gatineau, Quebec, Kristen Cote, chief technology officer of Edmonton-based Earth-observation company Wyvern, said launch access had become a question during fundraising discussions.Cote said.Canada has companies developing rockets and launch sites, but the report said none had yet launched anything into orbit.The Canadian government’s Launch the North competition is providing $25 million in incentives to three companies, prioritising smaller rockets.Those vehicles could carry only a limited number of satellites. They wouldn't offer the same capacity as Falcon 9 for deploying large satellite networks.One of Canada’s major satellite providers, Telesat, has booked SpaceX launches for its 225-satellite Lightspeed communications network before the anticipated Falcon 9 phaseout, according to the report. Those arrangements depend on the satellites being ready on schedule. CEO Dan Goldberg said Telesat needs a provider that can carry many satellites, launch frequently, and keep prices competitive.Goldberg said.Launches are expected to account for about 20 per cent of Lightspeed’s budget, or roughly US$1 billion. That makes the price of an alternative provider a substantial consideration.Maritime Launch Services’ site near Canso, Nova Scotia, has approvals for medium-lift rockets, according to CEO Stephen Matier. However, the company is not currently preparing for those launches.he said.Canada Rocket Company is developing a medium-lift vehicle. CEO Hugh Kolias estimated that preparing a new rocket for orbit takes six to eight years and costs about $1 billion. He said the company was targeting the shorter end of that timeline but wouldn't be ready by 2028.
Article Summary: Elon Musk’s SpaceX has reportedly stopped accepting launch bookings from Canadian companies. The reported cutoff concerns Falcon 9 missions beyond 2028. For Canadian satellite companies seeking investment to expand, the uncertainty is said to be prompting investors to question how their planned satellites will reach orbit.

Article Title: Bloodbath at Wall Street reminds of two warnings that Jamie Dimon long talked to JP Morgan shareholders about: Our balance sheet is …
Article Text:
JP Morgan CEO Jamie Dimon

What did Jamie Dimon mean by a ‘fortress balance sheet’

Why are investors questioning the AI giants' moats

AI spending is rising, but where are the returns

A sharp sell-off in technology stocks has brought two long-standing warnings from JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon back into focus. As investors question whether AI companies can protect their competitive advantages and justify their growing spending, Jamie Dimon's earlier comments about financial strength and business competition offer a reminder of the risks facing even the biggest companies. Dimon has repeatedly spoken to JPMorgan shareholders about the importance of having a “fortress balance sheet”. In his 2015 shareholder letter, he dedicated a section to explaining what the phrase meant. By 2021, he had added another warning, saying that “the moats that protect this company are not particularly deep”.Jamie Dimon's reference to a “fortress balance sheet” reflects his emphasis on maintaining financial strength and being prepared for difficult market conditions. As mentioned above, he discussed the phrase in his 2015 letter to JPMorgan shareholders, setting aside a section to explain its meaning. The idea is that a strong balance sheet can help a company withstand financial pressure rather than struggle when markets turn against it.His second warning, made in 2021, focused on the limits of competitive advantages.Jamie Dimon then said the moats protecting JPMorgan were “not particularly deep”.The term “moat” is commonly used in business to describe the advantages that protect a company from competitors.The idea was popularised by investor Warren Buffett . In a 1999 Fortune article with Carol Loomis, Buffett argued that a company's competitive advantage and how long it can maintain that advantage are key considerations for investors.The recent technology stock sell-off has raised questions about whether the biggest companies investing in AI can maintain their market positions while spending heavily on the technology.The decline began with Google-parent Alphabet. Its shares fell 12.6% on October 29 after its quarterly results showed that revenue from its core search business had fallen short of expectations. Its free cash flow also came in at negative $9.1 billion, compared with the negative $2.23 billion analysts had expected, according to FactSet.Software company ServiceNow dropped 27% on the same day following slower revenue growth and disappointing guidance. Amazon and Intel also came under pressure, with Intel falling roughly 25% before the market opened on Friday.The Financial Times calculated that Big Tech companies lost nearly $900 billion in market value after another sharp increase in AI spending during the third quarter. Nasdaq 100 companies lost more than $1 trillion in market value on Friday alone.One concern for investors is that AI could disrupt the businesses that currently generate significant cash for technology companies, even as those same companies spend more money building AI infrastructure. According to S&P Global Market Intelligence data cited in the Fortune report, major cloud companies raised $326 billion through stocks and bonds this year to fund their AI expansion. That is more than three times the amount raised in 2025.At the same time, the cost of using AI models is falling. OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Terra model reportedly costs up to half as much per token as the previous version. An index from expense-management company Ramp also showed token prices falling around 35% since the end of June, pointing to growing price competition.Apollo chief economist Torsten Slok has also questioned whether AI investments are delivering meaningful financial benefits to companies outside the technology sector. In an October 24 note, he argued that AI had delivered no financial payoff to corporate America outside tech.
Article Summary: Jamie Dimon has repeatedly spoken to JPMorgan shareholders about the importance of having a “fortress balance sheet” In his 2015 shareholder letter, he dedicated a section to explaining what the phrase meant. By 2021, he had added another warning, saying that “the moats that protect this company are not particularly deep’

Article Title: Next Week on Xbox: New Games coming on Microsoft gaming platform for November 2 to 6

Article Title: Godfather of AI Geoffrey Hinton says Google will win the AI race; those less likely to win are Microsoft and …
Article Text:
Godfather of AI Geoffrey Hinton

Geoffrey Hinton says Microsoft and Meta are less likely to win AI race

Why Geoffrey Hinton favours Google

Godfather of AI Geoffrey Hinton believes tech giant Google has a strong chance of winning the AI race, while Microsoft and Meta may be less likely to emerge as leaders. However, Hinton also acknowledged that his past association with Google could influence his view. "If I had to bet on one lot of people, it would probably be Google," Geoffrey Hinton said while sharing his views on which companies could lead the AI race. "But I used to work for Google, so don't take me too seriously about that. I have a vested interest in them winning," he further added.Hinton, who is widely known as the 'Godfather of AI' for his pioneering work in the field, also named Anthropic and OpenAI as companies that could challenge Google.While Geoffrey Hinton sees Google as a likely contender, he believes Microsoft and Meta have a lower chance of winning the AI race."Anthropic might win. OpenAI might win," he said. "I think it's less likely that Microsoft will win or that Facebook will win," Hinton added.Geoffrey Hinton also explained that the outcome may depend less on who leads a company and more on its ability to attract talented people and provide them with the resources needed to develop AI."It's not who's running it, it's who has the resources to get the right people to do the work."Geoffrey Hinton's comments come with an important qualification. He previously worked at Google, where he spent more than a decade researching artificial intelligence before leaving the company in 2023. He spent about 10 years working on artificial neural networks and deep learning technologies for Google. In 2012, his work (alongside his students) on AlexNet laid the technical foundation for modern generative AI and large language models.After leaving Google, Hinton was awarded the 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics for his foundational discoveries and inventions in machine learning with artificial neural networks.
Article Summary: Godfather of AI Geoffrey Hinton believes tech giant Google has a strong chance of winning the AI race. Hinton also named Anthropic and OpenAI as companies that could challenge Google. He previously worked at Google, where he spent more than a decade researching artificial intelligence before leaving in 2023.

Article Title: After donating more than $7 billion in 2025, MacKenzie Scott gave the Trevor Project $45 million as the LGBTQ+ youth organisation faced funding cuts and financial challenges
Article Text:
PC: The US News & World Report

MacKenzie Scott gives the Trevor Project its largest-ever donation

Trevor Project continues crisis support after losing federal funding

Trevor Project’s budget falls to $47 million after years of rapid growth

MacKenzie Scott’s record gift gives the Trevor Project room to plan ahead

Why MacKenzie Scott gives millions without requiring project proposals

A $45 million donation from billionaire philanthropist MacKenzie Scott has given the Trevor Project a substantial financial boost at a time when the LGBTQ+ youth organisation is adjusting to the loss of federal funding and a smaller operating budget. The gift, made towards the end of 2025, is the largest the nonprofit has received in its history. It also comes after several difficult years marked by leadership changes, staff reductions and questions about managing rapid growth. As reported by The US News & World Report, Scott had previously donated $6 million to the organisation in 2020. Her latest contribution arrives as the Trevor Project reassesses its finances and considers how best to maintain its crisis support services.The Trevor Project announced the gift on January 12, 2026, saying it had received the money from Scott at the end of the previous year. The organisation provides crisis intervention and suicide prevention support for LGBTQ+ young people, including through an independent hotline.For chief executive Jaymes Black, the size of the contribution came as a surprise. The nonprofit had been dealing with financial pressure, and the donation offered a significant addition to its resources at a time when its funding position had changed.Scott's philanthropy has attracted attention for the size of her grants and the way she distributes them. Her wealth largely originated from her divorce from Amazon founder Jeff Bezos. In 2025, she gave more than $7 billion to nonprofit organisations, according to figures reported by the Associated Press. The Trevor Project's $45 million gift was not included in the donations listed on her website in December.The Trevor Project lost $25 million in federal funding after the Trump administration ended a specialised option for LGBTQ+ young people using the 988 National Suicide & Crisis Lifeline in July 2025. The service had allowed callers to access support tailored to their needs, including those related to sexual orientation and gender identity.The nonprofit had been among the organisations providing that assistance. According to Black, it continued to reach around 250,000 young people each year through its own hotline. A further 250,000 callers had been served through the 988 option, known as Press 3, before that service ended.The US Department of Health and Human Services reported that more than 1.5 million contacts had been routed through the wider 988 service between September 2022 and July 2025. Those contacts covered the broader crisis line, rather than the Trevor Project alone.Scott Bertani, director of advocacy at the National Coalition for LGBTQ Health, said the organisation's services addressed needs that general crisis lines were not specifically designed to handle. Young people dealing with rejection, isolation or distress connected to their identity may seek support from a service with relevant experience, he said.The Trevor Project has continued operating its independent hotline since the federal programme ended. The loss of the additional option, however, has placed greater importance on the organisation's ability to sustain that work.The federal funding loss was not the organisation's only financial challenge. The Trevor Project's budget expanded sharply over several years, rising from about $4 million in 2016 to more than $83 million in 2023, according to its public tax returns. That growth coincided with internal difficulties, including a change in leadership and a series of staff cuts.The board removed the organisation's chief executive in 2022, and further layoffs followed, including reductions in July 2025. Black said the nonprofit's budget for 2026 stood at $47 million, considerably below its reported level in 2023, as reported The US News & World Report.Rapid expansion can create management pressures for charities as well as businesses. Thad Calabrese, a New York University professor who studies nonprofit financial management, said organisations that grow quickly can encounter financial problems. He also pointed to the wider uncertainty created when government support is reduced or withdrawn.Public funding has often been treated as a dependable source of income for nonprofits. Yet relying on it can leave organisations exposed when political priorities change. Calabrese said the recent instability in federal funding had disrupted the operating models of charities beyond the Trevor Project.Following the loss of federal support, the Trevor Project launched an emergency fundraising campaign. By the time of the Associated Press report in January 2026, the appeal had raised $20 million, according to Black.The campaign provided another source of support as the nonprofit worked through the immediate consequences of the funding cut. Black said the organisation hoped the fundraising effort had demonstrated its ability to continue through a difficult period.Scott's donation is intended to have a longer-term effect, rather than being tied to a specific project with a fixed spending schedule. Black said the donor's representatives had made clear that the contribution was designed to support lasting impact. The Trevor Project planned to take time to decide how the money should be used.The $45 million gift is larger than the Trevor Project's stated 2026 operating budget of $47 million only by a small margin, but its potential value will depend on how the money is managed over time. The donation does not, by itself, resolve the questions surrounding the nonprofit's future income or operating costs.Scott has become one of the most prominent individual philanthropists in the United States, in part because she frequently makes large donations without requiring recipients to spend the money on a narrowly defined project. Her giving has often supported organisations working on equity and social justice.Unlike many traditional grantmakers, Scott generally does not ask charities to submit project proposals or accept applications for funding. An open call in 2023 was an exception to that approach. Her team conducts its own assessment of potential recipients, although relatively little is publicly known about its internal selection process.The size of her donations has sometimes prompted questions about whether a charity can manage a sudden increase in resources without expanding too quickly or becoming dependent on an unusually large grant. Research from the Center for Effective Philanthropy, however, has found limited evidence that the concerns surrounding misuse of Scott's gifts or unsustainable growth have broadly materialised.
Article Summary: Billionaire philanthropist MacKenzie Scott gives Trevor Project its largest-ever donation. The LGBTQ+ youth organisation is adjusting to the loss of federal funding and a smaller operating budget. The gift, made towards the end of 2025, is the largest the nonprofit has received in its history.

Article Title: Digi Yatra begins international passenger trials at seven airports
Article Text: Digi Yatra has commenced trials for international passengers at seven airports across India, marking a further step in the adoption of digital technology in the country’s aviation sector.The trials, scheduled to run from November to December 2026, will allow eligible Indian nationals holding e-passports to use the Digi Yatra at designated airport touchpoints while travelling on select international flights operated by Air India and IndiGo.According to the Ministry of Civil Aviation, the trials are being conducted at Delhi, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Cochin, Mumbai, Chennai and Amritsar airports. Eligible passengers will be able to use the facility at terminal entry points, Security Hold Areas (SHA) and boarding gates, wherever the required infrastructure is available. Feedback received during the trial period will inform the planning of a wider rollout in 2027.To access the facility, eligible Indian nationals must create an e-passport-based Verifiable Credential (VC) through the Digi Yatra mobile application.The process involves scanning the Machine Readable Zone (MRZ) of the e-passport, reading the embedded chip using the Near Field Communication (NFC) feature of a compatible smartphone, capturing a selfie and verifying the details. The credential is stored in the passenger’s Digi Yatra wallet on the device and can be used at airport touchpoints enabled for the trials.The facility is intended to complement, and not replace, existing travel processes. Passengers must continue to carry their travel documents and complete all mandatory airline document checks, immigration procedures and other applicable travel formalities.The Digi Yatra’s adoption continues to expand across India’s aviation network. The platform has over 26.5 million users and has enabled more than 110 million journeys across 39 domestic airports, serving domestic airlines. A further 25 domestic airports are planned to be covered by 2027.The Ministry of Civil Aviation remains committed to leveraging technology to improve airport operations and facilitate seamless air travel, in line with the Government of India’s vision of Digital India and Ease of Flying. (ANI)
Article Summary: The trials are being conducted at Delhi, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Cochin, Mumbai, Chennai and Amritsar airports. Eligible passengers will be able to use the facility at terminal entry points, Security Hold Areas (SHA) and boarding gates, wherever the required infrastructure is available.

Article Title: As billion dollar valuations come crashing down under worries about AI demand; China sends a message to the world: AI bubble has already burst
Article Text:
China’s AI bubble bursts as STAR50 index wipes out $480 billion in four months

China's biggest AI stock debuts have lost half their value

One crowded AI trade dragged down China's whole market

China's AI stocks still look expensive after the selloff

China's artificial intelligence trade, the hottest bet on its stock market this year, has come apart in under four months. The STAR50 index, Shanghai's board of homegrown AI and chip leaders, has fallen about 40% from its July high, erasing roughly $480 billion in market value as worries over AI demand and curbs on Chinese exports caught up with stretched valuations.The collapse comes as Wall Street goes through its own AI scare. Alphabet shed about $500 billion in a single session on Thursday, Intel sank 28% on Friday and the Nasdaq ended October with its worst monthly slide since March 2025. While investors in New York debate whether the AI bubble is about to burst, China has already answered that question for itself.The pain goes well beyond tech. China's blue-chip CSI 300 index is down about 20% from its June peak, putting it in bear market territory, and Beijing pumped $19 billion into exchange-traded funds last week, its largest intervention since early 2025. "The stock market later evolved into a speculative crazy bull," Beijing-based fund manager Dong Baozhen told Reuters. "And now we see the bubble bursting."The names hit hardest were the market's darlings. Humanoid robot maker Unitree drew retail orders 8,000 times the shares on offer and surged 600% in its Shanghai debut in August, only to halve since. GPU makers MetaX and Moore Threads, seen as China's answer to Nvidia, jumped 700% and 400% on their first trading days last year and have also lost half their value since July.Memory chipmaker CXMT became Shanghai's most heavily weighted stock just three months after listing, and now sits nearly 30% below its August peak. Optical module suppliers Zhongji Innolight and Eoptolink trade around 60% under their summer highs, partly because Washington is moving to bar them from supplying US data centres.Chen Wensheng, a small business owner from Hainan, bought in because state-backed funds had invested in firms like Unitree, which he read as official support. He and his friends are now sitting on losses.There was no obvious trigger. Traders point to prices that had run too far, tax bills and the threat of overseas bans on Chinese data centre equipment. What made the fall so wide was concentration. Goldman Sachs estimates AI stocks make up 42% of China's market value and 57% of turnover across mainland and Hong Kong-listed shares, so when the theme turned, almost every portfolio felt it."The selloff reflects a repricing of crowded AI trades," Gary Ng, senior economist for Asia Pacific at Natixis, told CNN, pointing to "weak domestic demand, and the lack of stimulus" as well.Hong Kong has not escaped either. The Hang Seng is down more than 12% this year, while the Hang Seng Tech index has lost about 30%. Chinese equities have now fallen for ten straight weeks, a run never seen before. That stings households who moved savings into stocks during a five-year property slump, with roughly 70% of family wealth still tied to real estate.Even after the drop, the STAR50 trades at about 100 times trailing earnings, down from nearly 250 at its peak. The Nasdaq 100 sits closer to 30. Hong Hao, chief investment officer at Lotus Asset Management, told Reuters he expects the rout to stall many tech firms' plans to list.Not everyone is heading for the exit. Goldman Sachs still has Innolight and CXMT on its recommended list, and Wu Qing, chairman of the China Securities Regulatory Commission, has promised to keep markets stable while nudging listed firms toward buybacks. Strict capital controls also limit how far the damage can travel into global markets.That leaves the question the selloff started with. Meta, Alphabet, Oracle, Amazon and Microsoft are set to spend about $800 billion on AI this year, and US investors are already punishing earnings that fall short. Shanghai fund manager Wang Zhuo expects China's chipmakers to land in the same price war as every other Chinese manufacturer. "There's no exception," he told Reuters. "All bubbles inevitably burst."
Article Summary: China's artificial intelligence trade, the hottest bet on its stock market this year, has come apart in under four months. The STAR50 index, Shanghai's board of homegrown AI and chip leaders, has fallen about 40% from its July high. The collapse comes as Wall Street goes through its own AI scare.

Article Title: Jeff Bezos and wife Lauren Sanchez Bezos have donated $100 million to protect the world's most-endangered animals and plants; idea is to make sure …
Article Text:
Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sanchez

Jeff Bezos’ Earth Fund joins new global conservation alliance

‘We know how to bring species back from the brink’

What the money will do

Building on the Phoenix Species project

Filling a government gap

Part of Bezos' $10 billion climate and nature pledge

Amazon founder Jeff Bezos and his wife Lauren Sanchez Bezos have committed $100 million via the Bezos Earth Fund to help protect some of the world’s most endangered animals and plants, backing a new global initiative designed to prevent species from slipping into extinction. As reported by Fortune, the donation is part of a broader $500 million Species Recovery Alliance, which is a coalition of conservation organisations that was introduced at the COP17 UN biodiversity conference in Yerevan, Armenia. The managing director of the fund, Cristián Samper made the announcement about the donation by Bezos and Sanchez. The report further adds that the Earth Fund is contributing $100 million dollars in all.According to a report by Fortune, the Bezos Earth Fund is one of nine founding members of the newly launched Species Recovery Alliance, which aims to accelerate efforts to recover species classified by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) as endangered, critically endangered or extinct in the wild.The Earth Fund made the commitment of $100 million in support of conservation groups and local partners who are working towards rebuilding wildlife populations via a series of measures such as habitat restoration, captive breeding programmes, disease management and the control of invasive species.Instead of pooling the resources in a single fund, the alliance members will coordinate their efforts while directing grants independently. The initiative comes at a time when more than 49,500 species are listed as threatened with extinction on the IUCN Red List. The alliance also plans to focus on three highest-risk categories, which together account for more than 31,000 species.Cristián Samper, managing director and leader of nature solutions at the Bezos Earth Fund, said the primary challenge facing conservation groups is often not scientific knowledge but long-term financial support. “We know how to bring species back from the brink. What too many conservation teams lack is reliable funding to keep that work going,” Samper told Fortune. He noted that rebuilding wildlife populations can take years and interruptions in funding can jeopardise years of conservation progress. The alliance's stated goal is to ensure that species recovery projects receive sustained support, giving endangered animals and plants a better chance of long-term survival.Depending on the species, the work could include breeding animals in captivity and releasing them, restoring habitat, managing disease or controlling invasive species. Members plan to track progress using the IUCN Red List and its Green Status of Species. The target list is long. The IUCN says more than 49,500 species are threatened with extinction, and the three highest-risk categories that the alliance will fund together include more than 31,000 species. Samper said the world knows how to bring species back from the brink, and that what many conservation teams lack is reliable funding to keep the work going. He noted that rebuilding a population can take years and that a break in support can put hard-won progress at risk.The alliance builds on the Phoenix Species Project, which the Earth Fund launched in August with Re:wild, the conservation group co-founded by DiCaprio. Each organisation committed $100 million, for a total of $200 million. The project aims to recover 100 critically endangered and extinct-in-the-wild species across 30 countries, including Madagascar’s golden-crowned sifaka and Australia’s elusive night parrot. Sánchez Bezos said at the time that children fall in love with animals before anyone tells them those animals are disappearing, and that the project is the couple’s answer to what to tell them when species like the night parrot or the sifaka are gone.The announcement comes amid growing concerns that governments are falling short of global biodiversity funding commitments. Countries agreed at the 2022 biodiversity summit in Montreal to mobilise $200 billion annually by 2030 for biodiversity protection. However, recent data cited in the report shows global funding levels remain well below that target.Samper said philanthropic organisations can help accelerate species recovery efforts, but added that large-scale and sustained public funding remains essential for long-term success.Alongside the private-sector alliance, 17 governments have launched the Coalition of Action to Recover Endangered Species (CARES), aimed at stepping up protection efforts for vulnerable wildlife populations.Bezos, the Amazon founder, launched the Earth Fund in 2020 with a $10 billion pledge to fight climate change and protect nature by 2030, which Fortune describes as the largest individual philanthropic commitment to climate and nature ever. The fund has granted $2.4 billion so far, a spokesperson said, leaving more than $7 billion to distribute in about four years. Fund officials told Bloomberg in May that they remain committed to the target. Sánchez Bezos, the fund’s vice chair since its early days, has become a more visible face of the couple’s giving.Recent announcements include $34 million for sustainable fabrics, $26 million for wildfire detection, $100 million to turn vacant urban land into parks in eight US cities, and more than $25 million in Pacific Ocean grants in September.
Article Summary: The Bezos Earth Fund is one of nine founding members of the newly launched Species Recovery Alliance. The alliance aims to accelerate efforts to recover species classified by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) as endangered, critically endangered or extinct in the wild. The initiative comes at a time when more than 49,500 species are listed as threatened with extinction on the IUCN Red List.
